title: Westphalia
hook: Two treaty cities ended the Thirty Years’ War; imperial institutions continued afterwards.
notes: Overlay: Reilly/Benedicti, Karte von der Deutschland, Vienna 1796, Rumsey 11151.021. Approximate georeferencing with city/coast controls; retained hand-coloured divisions are the mapmaker’s portrayal, not reconstructed polygons. Credit David Rumsey Map Collection, David Rumsey Map Center, Stanford University Libraries. Adaptation CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. Fine print is supplemented by readable modern annotations; a close view deliberately shows only part of the empire. Westphalia primary treaty text and Habsburger peace history; UNESCO Regensburg. Calendar note: the primary treaties are dated 14/24 October 1648 (Julian/Gregorian); scene years avoid silently selecting one day style. Coordinates are approximate named-place locators, not imported surveyed points. Modern borders are hidden. Event cards contain claim-level citations. The later term Holy Roman Empire must not be projected unchanged onto Charlemagne’s Frankish realm.

scenes.title: Two cities, related negotiations
scenes.text: Münster and Osnabrück hosted the peace settlements with France and Sweden in 1648. Their proximity makes Westphalia a concrete diplomatic geography, not the name of a single signing table.

scenes.title: Religion and imperial law
scenes.text: The treaties addressed confessional rights and relations among imperial estates. The institutional anchor at Regensburg locates the empire’s assembly world; it does not mark where the treaties were signed.

scenes.title: Peace did not dissolve the empire
scenes.text: Regensburg’s Perpetual Diet began in 1663 and continued until 1806. Moving beyond 1648 makes the continuing institutional geography visible.

scenes.title: A much later territorial view
scenes.text: The 1796 Reilly map shows the empire’s territorial complexity long after Westphalia. It is expressly not a map of the 1648 settlement and cannot be used to read off its immediate border changes.
